title: Renewal Decline Root Cause Matrix & Counterfactual Playbook
content:
Purpose: Provide a lightweight, reproducible template for running a renewal-decline (loss) postmortem focused on: 1) surface-level reasons, 2) evidence/triage timeline, and 3) concrete counterfactual hypotheses + experiments that could change the outcome. Use this during weekly CS retro or immediately after a documented churn event.

How to use (quick):
- Owner fills high-level summary within 48 hours of confirmed decline.
- Gather signals (usage, support, billing, sales notes) within 5 business days.
- Run 30–60 minute exit interview with key contacts where possible.
- Triage into Root Cause Matrix and select 1–3 prioritized counterfactuals to A/B test for similar at-risk accounts.

Snapshot summary (example):
- Account: Keystone Analytics (example)
- ARR at risk: $38,400
- Renewal decision date: 2026-01-30
- Decline reason reported: "cost + model accuracy drift for inference"
- Primary evidence: usage down 47% over last 2 months, 3 support tickets about latency/timeout, no dedicated meeting in Q4.

Root Cause Matrix (fill for each lost account)
Columns: Category | Observed signals | Why we think it mattered | Leading indicator severity (low/med/high) | Evidence links (ticket ids, query snapshots)
- Product fit | sudden drop in API qps, feature usage off by >30% | new model changed prompt behavior -> accuracy mismatch | high | TICKET-452, REDSHIFT-usage-export-01.csv
- Pricing/Cost | customer cites cost during exit; spike in token spend per inference | heavy batched workloads after prototype -> per-call costs rose | med | Billing-2026-Q1-export.csv
- Reliability/Latency | multiple 5xx/timeout incidents, slow tail latency | backend timeouts impacted user workflows during peak | high | SRE-incident-453, logs/trace/abc123
- Relationship/Engagement | last exec check-in 6 months ago; no success plan updates | contact rotation; new user not onboarded | med | calendar/Keystone-exec-2025
- Competitive | customer evaluating vendor X for lower cost and managed fine-tuning | competitor offered offline fine-tune and private endpoint | low | Sales-notes: opp-987
- Security/Compliance | requested on-prem or VPC; we didn't offer desired profile | procurement blocked due to data residency concerns | med | procurement-email-thread-xx

Counterfactual Hypotheses (structured):
- Hypothesis ID: H-01
- Hypothesis text: If we had proactively modeled and surfaced per-team token trend alerts and recommended quantization profiles, the customer would not have faced a cost shock and might have renewed.
- Evidence supporting: steep rise in per-token cost for inference routes; no pre-sale guidance on quantization applied.
- Experiment to validate: build a dashboard and automated email for accounts with >20% qps increase and token spend >$X/month; pilot for 8 accounts identified as "at-risk-by-cost". 3-month metric: reduction in churn for cohort.
- Owner: Diego Morales
- Priority: P1

- Hypothesis ID: H-02
- Hypothesis text: If we had scheduled an operations review and a canary test for the model update, we’d have detected quality regression sooner and provided a fallback, preventing the product-fit loss.
- Evidence supporting: timing of model rollout aligns with drop in usage and support tickets reporting lower accuracy.
- Experiment to validate: require canary checks + golden prompt eval in release checklist; instrument a rollback play for dedicated customers.
- Owner: Priya Shah
- Priority: P2

Exit Interview Script (30–45 min, informal, record with permission)
- Opening (5 min): thanks, goal is to learn; won't argue decision.
- Context (5 min): confirm account org, who uses the product, what changed since last renewal.
- Experience questions (10–15 min):
  - Can you walk me through how teams use Redwood today (most common flows)?
  - What were the top 2–3 pain points in the last 6 months?
  - Were there specific incidents or a slow decline? Which mattered more?
  - How did cost/latency/accuracy influence your decision? Be concrete (examples, dates).
- Competitive/procurement questions (5 min):
  - Did another product provide something we didn’t?
  - Was procurement blocked by a specific policy (data residency, security)?
- Counterfactual thinking (5–10 min):
  - If we fixed X in the next 30 days (X = example: 10–15% lower cost path, one-week QA rollback), would that change your decision?
  - What timeline or guarantees would be persuasive?
- Close: ask for permission to follow-up, who else we should speak to, any artifacts they can share.

Data sources to collect (practical):
- Product telemetry exports: monthly and last-90-day API qps, per-route token spend, embedding calls, tail latency distribution (p95/p99).
- Billing exports: invoice line items, per-route attribution if available.
- Support & SRE: ticket exports, incident timelines, runbook actions.
- Sales & AE notes: last 12 months of meeting notes, SOWs, renewal terms.
- Contract/procurement: signed SOW, termination clauses, required security reviews.

Triage timeline template (example cadence):
- Day 0–2: Confirm churn reason, assign owner, export quick signals (usage, billing, open tickets).
- Day 3–7: Conduct exit interview (or at least a summary call), populate Root Cause Matrix and evidence.
- Week 2: Convene cross-functional 30–60m postmortem: CS, Sales, SRE, Product. Agree top 3 counterfactuals and owners.
- Week 3–12: Run experiments (dashboards, alerts, small feature toggles, pricing pilot) and log outcomes.
- 90 days: Review cohort-level effect for similar accounts; update QBR playbooks.

Postmortem follow-up checklist (must-haves):
- [ ] Short public summary for internal CS channel (1–2 paragraphs).
- [ ] Root cause matrix completed + evidence links attached.
- [ ] At least one counterfactual with owner and measurable success metric.
- [ ] Ticket or engineering task created for any product fixes; link added.
- [ ] Billing/finance review if pricing was material (adjust billing mapping or offer pilot credits).
- [ ] Update churn taxonomy tags in CRM (reason/category) and add to retention dashboard.

Examples (filled, synthetic)
- Keystone Analytics (fictional):
  - Loss category: Product fit + Pricing
  - Observed signals: spike in tail latency (p99), per-call token cost doubled after a new feature adoption, 2 public support escalations.
  - Counterfactual prioritized: provide a temporary dedicated capacity trial + cost-smoothing credit for 90 days.
  - Result (experiment): pilot offered to three similar accounts in Q3; 2 renewed (small n, early signal).

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we normalize "per-call token cost" across model variants in billing export to make signal detection easier? (YES — finance + infra to discuss mapping)
- How to automate discovery of model rollouts tied to customer infra (we have release tags but need better mapping to customer clusters).
- Consider adding a small field in CRM for "earliest at-risk signal date" so we can measure time-to-detection vs time-to-decline.

Suggested KPIs to track for postmortem program:
- Mean time from at-risk signal to owner assignment (goal < 48 hours).
- % lost accounts with at least one counterfactual attempted (goal > 40% within 30 days).
- Cohort churn delta after experiment (primary outcome for prioritized experiments).

Appendix: quick templates (copy-paste)
- Internal summary (for #cs-retros):
  - Account: {{account_name}} | ARR: {{arr}} | Decision: Declined on {{date}} | Primary drivers: {{top3 reasons}} | Owner: {{owner}}
\- Email to request exit interview:
  - Subject: Quick follow-up on your renewal decision
  - Body: Hi {{contact_first}}, thanks for the transparent conversation earlier. We aim to learn — could we book 30 minutes this week to understand if there are specific changes we could make in the next 90 days that would be meaningful? No sales pressure, just listening. Best, {{owner}}

Versioning / ownership
- Template owner: Aisha Patel (CS Ops)
- Suggested reviewers: Product-hosted-api, Finance, SRE
- Next review: 2026-05-01

End of doc.
